title: Euler product
statement: Factorization of a Dirichlet series over prime axes for multiplicative coefficients.

title: Mobius inversion
statement: F=1*f implies f=mu*F over divisor sums.

title: Hyperbola method
statement: Split a divisor-type sum around sqrt(x) into two regions.

title: Perron / contour integral
statement: Turn a partial sum into a contour integral, shift the contour, collect residues.

title: Character orthogonality
statement: 1_{n=a mod q} = phi(q)^{-1} sum_chi conj(chi(a)) chi(n).

title: Halasz distance
statement: Mean value of a bounded multiplicative function controlled by pretentious distance to n^{it}.

title: Delange mean value criterion
statement: Mean value of a bounded multiplicative function via a convergent prime series criterion.

title: Wirsing theorem
statement: Mean values of non-negative multiplicative functions with controlled prime averages.

title: Selberg-Delange method
statement: Mean values when F(s)=zeta(s)^z G(s) with z suitable; Euler-singularity engine.

title: Turan-Kubilius inequality
statement: Variance bound for additive functions; concentration certificate.

title: Erdos-Kac theorem
statement: omega(n) is asymptotically Gaussian with mean and variance loglog n.

title: Generation / step recursion (certificate discipline)
statement: Structures built by generation from a base under rules; step induction proves properties over generated structures, step recursion defines functions out of them (valid only when the generation is free). Governance/certificate discipline for generated objects, not a universal proof tool.

title: Formal deduction system (certificate discipline)
statement: A deduction is a formal proof object: a finite, rule-checkable derivation from premises over a fixed formal language; validity depends on syntax, allowed rules, premises, and steps, not on the conclusion's plausibility. Governance/certificate tool, not a universal proof engine.

title: Completeness (syntax-semantics bridge, certificate discipline)
statement: Completeness (Godel): semantic consequence is captured by formal derivation under the certified system - Gamma |= phi implies Gamma |- phi. Governance/certificate tool: certifies the derivation system is adequate to semantic consequence; it does NOT promise that every mathematical truth is derivable in any fixed theory. Not a proof engine.

title: Compactness (local-to-global, certificate discipline)
statement: Compactness: a set of sentences is globally satisfiable iff every finite subset is satisfiable - global satisfiability is certified through finite satisfiability within the certified logic. Governance/certificate tool: local-to-global for satisfiability; it does NOT certify truth of the intended (infinite) structure, and is not a tool for solving open problems. Not a proof engine.

title: Character-sum phase reading (residue-fiber)
statement: Reads Dirichlet character sums as residue-fiber phase observables (via orthogonality). Observable/diagnostic technique; not a new character theorem, not a PNT/AP improvement, not RH/GRH.

title: L(s,chi) as residue-fiber generating object
statement: Reads L(s,chi) as a residue-fiber generating/organizing object: an Euler product / Dirichlet series packaging character-weighted arithmetic information across residue classes. Generating/organizing object, not a new L-function theorem, not a proof engine; control of its zeros stays GRH-level (MC-005, unsolved).

title: Zero-density estimate as diagnostic tool
statement: Reads classical zero-density estimates N(sigma,T) (bounds on the number of zeros with real part >= sigma up to height T) as a frontier diagnostic and conditional/average substitute for RH in error terms. Diagnoses the density-hypothesis wall; not RH/GRH progress, not a PNT/AP improvement, not a new theorem.

title: Large-value / mean-value machinery as diagnostic tool
statement: Reads large-value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials and mean-value (second-moment) theorems as diagnostic support feeding zero-density bounds N(sigma,T). The large-sieve inequality is the ambient mean-value inequality (not ingested as a separate unit here). Conditional/average support; not RH/GRH progress, not a large-values theorem, not a PNT/AP improvement, not a new result.

title: Prime-detecting sieve as information consumption
statement: Reads a prime-detecting sieve (Harman's method) as information consumption: which arithmetic information (Type-I linear/smooth vs Type-II bilinear) the sieve consumes to detect primes, and where the parity barrier and the unconditional sieve ceiling bite. Diagnostic; not a new prime detector, not parity-breaking, not a theorem improvement, not RH/GRH progress.

title: Type-I / Type-II information and Harman decomposition
statement: Reads Type-I (linear, level-of-distribution) vs Type-II (bilinear, well-factorable) information as a diagnostic of what a sieve consumes and what it lacks; Harman's decomposition shows which pieces are Type-I-handleable and which residue needs external Type-II. Type-II is the missing external certificate that would cross parity, not obtainable from remainders. Diagnostic; not a parity-breaking certificate by itself, not a prime detector, not a theorem improvement, not RH/GRH progress.
